descriptor: Consumer Retail / Membership Warehouse Club · FY ends 31 August · reported in USD

sections.title: Membership & Warehouse Growth
sections.subtitle: membership fees are almost pure margin and fund the thin markup on merchandise -- renewal rate and member count matter more here than any P&L line

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Costco Wholesale Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

comparableSales.title: Comparable sales growth
comparableSales.content:
Comparable sales (comps) is revenue growth at warehouses open at least a year, stripped of new-store openings and (for the headline number) currency and gasoline price swings -- the cleanest read on whether existing clubs are selling more.

For Costco: comps, not new warehouse openings, drive most of the model's growth -- the chain adds only a few dozen warehouses a year against ~900 already open. E-commerce consistently outgrows the in-warehouse business and is the fastest-growing segment, though it is still a small share of the total.

What to watch:

  • Total-company comps decelerating even as e-commerce holds up (a traffic problem, not a mix problem)
  • US vs. Other International divergence -- international comps are more exposed to FX translation
  • Gas price swings distorting the ex-FX-ex-gas line versus the headline number

membershipBase.title: Membership base
membershipBase.content:
Total cardholders is every member; paid household members are the primary membership accounts that each pay the annual fee; Executive members pay a higher fee (Executive) for a 2% reward on spend and are the most profitable tier.

For Costco: membership fees are close to 100% margin and have historically been roughly two-thirds of operating income -- member growth matters as much as comps for the model, and the Executive mix shift (more Executive members generally raises average fee yield) is a lever management calls out every quarter.

What to watch:

  • Paid member growth outrunning or lagging new warehouse openings
  • Executive members as a rising share of total paid members
  • Cardholders (includes add-on cards) growing faster than paid primary members, which would flatter the headline without adding fee revenue

membershipFee.title: Membership fee revenue and renewal rate
membershipFee.content:
Membership fee revenue is the annual fee income recognised over the membership year. The renewal rate is the share of memberships up for renewal in the period that actually renew -- Costco's clearest read on member satisfaction and switching cost.

For Costco: renewal rates above 90% in the US & Canada (and high-80s worldwide, dragged down by newer international markets) are the moat the valuation leans on -- a 1-point move in renewal rate is a bigger swing in recurring, high-margin revenue than a point of merchandise margin.

What to watch:

  • Worldwide renewal rate converging toward (or diverging from) the more mature US & Canada rate as international clubs age
  • Fee revenue growth outpacing paid-member growth (a fee increase or Executive mix shift) versus just tracking it

storeCount.title: Warehouse count by region
storeCount.content:
Total open warehouses, split between the US, Canada and Other International (the rest of the world).

For Costco: new warehouses are the main unit-growth lever (alongside comps) and each one carries years of built-in membership and sales growth as it matures -- the pace and geographic mix of openings signals where management sees runway. The US base is largely saturated; Other International is the higher-growth, lower-margin-at-first expansion front.

What to watch:

  • Net new warehouses per year relative to the ~900-strong existing base (a slowing rate of openings)
  • Other International's growing share of the total, and whether comps there keep pace with new-store dilution
